iterations.disagreement_summary: The largest disagreement mass sat in phase (kappa 0.458): classifier-1 anchored on the layer where a failure surfaced or was handled, while classifier-2 anchored on the artifact in which the defect lives, splitting repeatedly on instrument/recording defects (worker verify vs reviewer build), external-tool runtime crashes and environment traps (worker build/verify vs reviewer ops), and protocol-design defects (worker verify vs reviewer spec). cause_class disagreements (kappa 0.728) concentrated on verification_gap acting as a catch-all: two document-vs-reality mismatches (P5-F-079, P5-F-083) and two unaccounted token burns (P5-F-027, P5-F-081) were labeled verification_gap by classifier-1 where classifier-2 applied spec_drift and resource_blindness, with two value-precision cases (P5-F-001, P5-F-106) splitting toward precision_overclaim and one gate-failure case (P5-F-043) splitting the other way. detection_layer was near-ceiling (kappa 0.946) with a single split on P5-F-066, where the steward catching its own validator's defects was read as self_caught by classifier-1 and reviewer_caught by classifier-2.
iterations.reviewer_verdict: APPROVE-WITH-FIXES (iteration-1 work order: 4 minor fixes, taxonomy revision per disagreement structure, reclassification of the 40 sample records under the revised schema)

iterations.disagreement_summary: Iteration-1 disagreement was confined to the phase field (6 of 40 rows; cause_class and detection_layer passed, detection at perfect agreement). Per Reviewer-1's report as relayed by the orchestrator, the six splits concentrated on four boundary patterns: a blocking capability/tool absence read as build by classifier-1 vs ops by classifier-2 (the F-051 WiX-type case); a quota/cap mis-enforced by runner code read as verify by classifier-1 (runner-as-instrument) vs build by classifier-2 (F-077-type); a determinism proof embedding stale recorded hashes labeled build by classifier-1 despite the v1.1 literal already assigning stale recorded hashes in proofs to verify - an application error by classifier-1, not a schema defect (the F-084 case); and the anchoring pair where a check session degraded by external conditions with controls intact belongs to verify (F-065-type, agreed) while an obtained external artifact that is not what it claims belongs to ops (F-116-type, split). Classifier-1 did not read the sealed classifier-2 file; this summary transcribes Reviewer-1's report and the work-order instruction, and the remaining rows of the six are of the same four patterns.

decision_rule_changes.old_rule: phase anchored on where the failure originated OR surfaced; verify included 'pilots failing their gates' and measurement-adjacent failures generally
decision_rule_changes.new_rule: phase anchored strictly on WHERE THE DEFECT LIVES (the spec/build/verify/ops artifact or process that is defective), not where it surfaced or was caught
worked_examples_added: value-recording registries/summaries built wrong (e.g. ERR transcribed as hits:0) -> verify
external-tool runtime crashes (e.g. pinned converter ValueError at load) -> ops
run/service configs that mis-budget resources (e.g. frozen max_tokens vs thinking-token burn) -> build
path/OS traps at execution (e.g. MSYS /tmp vs native Python) -> ops
document-content defects (stale figures, wrong pointers, rule != behavior) -> spec

decision_rule_changes.old_rule: verification_gap defined broadly (missing, untested, unexercised, or too coarse checking) and effectively served as the residual class
decision_rule_changes.new_rule: verification_gap narrowed to checking-shaped defects only, reached via an explicit 9-step tie-break order; three boundary rules encoded with worked examples: ERR-count transcribed as hits:0 -> precision_overclaim (P5-F-063-type); document-vs-reality mismatch -> spec_drift (P5-F-079/F-083-type); unaccounted token burn -> resource_blindness (P5-F-027/F-081-type)
worked_examples_added: opt-in ctx guard / param added but never exercised / unwired degradation path -> verification_gap (stays)
documented record_id rule verifies 0/94 records -> spec_drift
thinking-mode burn against frozen max_tokens -> resource_blindness

decision_rule_changes.old_rule: other:credential-exposure carried as PROPOSED class with 1 member
decision_rule_changes.new_rule: PROMOTED to full class credential_exposure: secret/credential exposed to observation without confirmed compromise; duty = rotation/hygiene; never reproduce the secret. Dual-classifier iteration-0 agreement 1.0 on the sole member (P5-F-033); proposed_classes_active now empty
worked_examples_added: owner HF Read token visible on-screen during login setup, rotation recommended and still open -> credential_exposure

decision_rule_changes.old_rule: reviewer_caught = 'first caught by a separate context: adversarial reviewer, data steward, gatekeeper' (ambiguous for steward-own-tool cases)
decision_rule_changes.new_rule: clarified: a steward/reviewer-role agent catching defects in its OWN tooling is self_caught relative to that tool (the owner of the failed thing is whoever produced it); reviewer_caught requires a genuinely separate second context over the owner's artifact. Worked example added both ways (steward validator self-catch vs worker builder caught by reviewer audit). NOTE: this is classifier-1's proposed reading of the single iteration-0 detection split (P5-F-066); the iteration-1 kappa decides it
worked_examples_added: steward's validator flags 3 FAILs that are all validator defects, caught on the steward's own rerun -> self_caught
worker's item-builder defect caught by the adversarial reviewer's scripted audit -> reviewer_caught
